new_wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Proof
new_wording.instruction: Do not use phrases that promise specific medical, cosmetic, or physiological results (e.g., reducing wrinkles, curing acne, balancing hormones, or whitening skin) unless you have a matching scientific fact and compliance sign-off. General descriptions of ingredients, mechanisms, or sensory experiences are allowed if they do not promise a specific outcome. If a claim implies a change in the body or skin condition, it must be backed by evidence.
examples_good: Contains niacinamide to help support skin barrier function.
Formulated with a unique blend of botanical extracts.
Provides a cooling sensation upon application.
examples_bad: Clinically proven to reduce wrinkles in 4 weeks.
Helps balance hormones and soothes migraines.

new_wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Proof
new_wording.instruction: Do not use phrases that promise specific medical, physiological, or comparative results (e.g., 'clinically proven,' 'cures,' 'reduces anxiety,' 'more effective than') unless you have the matching scientific fact and compliance sign-off on file. General descriptive benefits that do not promise a specific measurable outcome or medical cure are allowed. If a claim implies a specific change in the body or compares performance against competitors, it must be backed by verified evidence.
examples_good: Helps hydrate dry skin for a smoother feel.
Contains natural botanical extracts for daily care.
Designed to support your morning routine.
examples_bad: Clinically proven to reduce wrinkles in 2 weeks.
More effective than traditional toothpaste for whitening.
Cures acne and prevents future breakouts.
